basis.governing_question: Which ERP should replace Farmácias Lusas's finance, purchasing and inventory systems, and how is it migrated and rolled out to 40 pharmacies and 2 warehouses?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Map requirements and process fit for finance, purchasing and inventory across the pharmacies and warehouses.

gate.label: Requirements sign-off
gate.decision: Approve the requirements and go to vendor selection?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Score ERP vendors against the requirements and build the business case for the vendor that fits best.

gate.label: Vendor selection
gate.decision: Which ERP vendor goes forward into implementation?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Configure the ERP, migrate data, and take it live from a pilot site to all pharmacies and warehouses.

gate.label: Final acceptance
gate.decision: Approve the ERP as running in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses?

workstreams.name: Process area requirements
workstreams.answers: What must the ERP do for finance, purchasing and inventory in the pharmacies and warehouses?
activities: Interview the people who run each process area
Map finance and purchasing together, then inventory
Consolidate the requirements for sign-off

workstreams.name: Current systems fit-gap
workstreams.answers: Where do today's finance, purchasing and inventory systems fall short of those requirements?
activities: Walk through today's systems with the people who use them
Review system documents and operational data
Compare each requirement with what today's systems do

workstreams.name: ERP vendor scoring
workstreams.answers: Which ERP vendors fit the signed-off requirements, and how do they score against them?
activities: Shortlist ERP vendors against the signed-off requirements
Run vendor demonstrations with process owners
Score each vendor against the requirements

workstreams.name: ERP business case
workstreams.answers: Does the business case for the best-fitting vendor support selecting it?
activities: Estimate costs and benefits of the best-fitting vendor
Check cost assumptions against operational data
Set out the case for the selection decision

workstreams.name: ERP configuration
workstreams.answers: Can the chosen ERP be configured and tested for finance, purchasing and inventory?
activities: Configure finance and purchasing together
Configure inventory once the first two areas are tested
Test each area with the people who run the process

workstreams.name: Data migration
workstreams.answers: Can data from today's systems be migrated and loaded into the ERP in a rehearsal?
activities: Map data from today's systems to the ERP
Clean and load data, finance and purchasing first
Run a migration rehearsal and check the results

workstreams.name: Pilot site go-live
workstreams.answers: Does the ERP run live and stable at a pilot site?
activities: Launch the ERP at a pilot site after the readiness review
Track stability with the site's staff and operational data
Log and fix issues before the rollout decision

workstreams.name: Site rollout waves
workstreams.answers: Can the ERP go live in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses, wave by wave?
activities: Roll out the ERP wave by wave to pharmacies and warehouses
Support each wave until it is stable
Confirm the ERP runs in all pharmacies and warehouses

deliverables.name: Requirements and fit-gap pack for sign-off
Fit-gap of current systems against requirements
Vendor shortlist against the signed-off requirements
ERP business case with vendor scoring for selection
Tested ERP configuration for finance and purchasing
Data migration rehearsal results and load checks
Pilot site go-live record with stability log
First rollout wave go-live and stability report
Final acceptance pack with go-live record by site

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Agree access to data and people
events.decision: Confirm access to system data and process owners for the requirements work?
agenda: Present the engagement approach and phases
Align on the data and people the diagnostic needs
Confirm access to system data and process owners

events.label: Check-in: requirements
events.decision: Confirm which finance and purchasing requirements go into the sign-off pack?
agenda: Present the finance and purchasing requirements draft
Discuss gaps and open items by process area
Confirm which requirements go into the sign-off pack

events.label: Requirements sign-off
events.decision: Approve the requirements and go to vendor selection?
agenda: Present the requirements and fit-gap pack
Review fit-gap of current systems against requirements
Decide whether to approve and go to vendor selection

events.label: Check-in: vendor scoring
events.decision: Which scored vendors go into the business case for the selection gate?
agenda: Present the vendor shortlist and scoring
Discuss scoring gaps between vendors
Decide which vendors go into the business case

events.label: Vendor selection
events.decision: Which ERP vendor goes forward into implementation?
agenda: Present the ERP business case and vendor scoring
Discuss business case results by vendor
Decide which vendor goes into implementation

events.label: Check-in: configuration
events.decision: Confirm the tested finance and purchasing setup as the migration baseline?
agenda: Present the tested finance and purchasing configuration
Review test results and open defects
Confirm the setup as the migration baseline

events.label: Workshop 1: pilot readiness
events.decision: Go or no-go on taking the pilot site live with the tested setup?
agenda: Review the tested inventory configuration
Review data migration rehearsal results and load checks
Decide whether the pilot site goes live

events.label: Workshop 2: rollout start
events.decision: Go or no-go on starting the rollout waves at the remaining sites?
agenda: Present the pilot go-live record and stability log
Discuss open issues from the pilot site
Decide whether the rollout waves start

events.label: Check-in: rollout stability
events.decision: Proceed with the remaining rollout waves as planned, or adjust them?
agenda: Present the first wave go-live and stability report
Decide whether the remaining waves proceed as planned
Align on the evidence needed for final acceptance

events.label: Final acceptance
events.purpose: Accept the ERP across all sites
events.decision: Approve the ERP as running in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses?
agenda: Present the final acceptance pack by site
Review go-live status of each pharmacy and warehouse
Decide whether to approve the ERP as running

architect_notes: Engagement length is not given, so every duration is an estimate to confirm before quoting.
Implementation takes the middle of a 23 to 34 week estimate; it reaches the top if areas take 6 weeks and waves 3 weeks.
Implementation is added to the technology selection archetype's Diagnostic and Design because the brief includes data migration and rollout to 40 pharmacies and 2 warehouses.
Design assumes shortlist and demonstrations without a formal tender; a tender would add 4 to 6 weeks and should be confirmed.

sub_questions.question: What must the ERP do for finance, purchasing and inventory, and where do today's systems fall short?
Which ERP fits the requirements, and does its business case support selecting it?
Can the ERP be configured, tested and loaded with migrated data for finance, purchasing and inventory?
Can the ERP run live and stable at a pilot site, then in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses?

drivers.evidence: roll it out to its 40 pharmacies and 2 warehouses

phases.name: Diagnostic

work.unit: Process area mapped with its requirements

phases.why: Three process areas mapped two at a time, plus start-up and synthesis weeks; inside the archetype's typical 3 to 6 weeks.

phases.name: Design
phases.why: One shortlist, demonstration and scoring round, then a synthesis week; no formal tender assumed. Inside the archetype's typical 4 to 8 weeks.

phases.name: Implementation

work.unit: System configured and tested for one process area
Rollout wave of up to 10 sites

phases.why: Areas configured two at a time, then one migration rehearsal, one pilot site and five rollout waves of up to 10 sites, in sequence.

sizing.levers: Rollout waves two at a time would save 4 to 6 weeks; configuring all three process areas together would save 4 to 6 more.
